conclusions: No actionable correctness or scope defect found in the two-file exact-head diff.

The fix preserves native fs.existsSync(sourcePath) and changes only the returned module ID. POSIX separators remain unchanged; Windows native backslashes become slash-separated IDs, matching the observed Core-relative-import identity.

The test executes the real configured prefix, resolver function, and plugin object from astro.config.mjs; it does not copy the normalization implementation into the test. The current Vite plugins array includes that same object.

The VM retains host path.join, real repository URL, real fs.readFileSync, real manifest existence checks, and actual packages/core/package.json exports. It stubs the final path.resolve and source-existence boundary to model native POSIX/Windows results without pretending to run native Windows.

The Windows expected value requires forward slashes and the mock returns backslashes. The normalization therefore cannot be supplied accidentally by the mocked path resolver. Recorded unchanged assertions fail on baseline Windows and pass on candidate; POSIX passes in both logs.

Source extraction is coupled to two local config markers. Current markers bound the complete resolver/plugin block; a missing start or moved end normally yields a ReferenceError or SyntaxError, not silent success. This small maintenance coupling is not an actionable defect in this bounded change.

path.resolve ignores its arguments in the fixture, so this test alone does not verify export-target mapping, general filesystem semantics, plugin registration, actual Vite/Rollup canonicalization, or native production behavior. Those are honest fixture boundaries and are covered separately where acceptance requires them.

C-AS-HOOK-0001, C-AS-HOOK-0002, P-BASE-DIALOG-CONTENT, and P-BASE-DIALOG-MASK are draft at the reviewed head. The change restores the website realization without changing those semantics or claiming lifecycle promotion.

No Core context/global singleton workaround, AsHook setup escape, dependency change, global dedupe policy, API/export change, generated-file change, or unrelated modification appears in the exact diff.
